career_overview.short_description: Design and build 2D and 3D interactive video games using game engines, physics, audio, and gameplay programming.
responsibilities: Program core gameplay loops, player movement controllers, and input handling
Implement 2D and 3D physics collisions, triggers, and raycasting
Build game state machines, inventory systems, and save/load persistence
Integrate game sound effects, background music, and user interface HUDs
Profile frame rates, optimize memory and draw calls, and export release builds
representative_work: A completed playable 2D/3D action or platformer game featuring player controls, enemy AI, collision physics, health/scoring UI, sound effects, and multi-level progression.
core_skills: Game engine architecture and game loops
Player movement, gravity, and input systems
Finite state machines for character behaviors
Sprite animation controllers and blend trees
Game audio: spatial sound effects and background music
Canvas HUDs: health bars, menus, and inventory
Game state saving, loading, and scene transitions
Frame rate profiling and draw call optimization

roadmap.title: Game Developer: beginner foundations and starter project
roadmap.intended_learner: Motivated beginner; basic computer literacy assumed, with no prior professional experience.
roadmap.starting_requirements: Computer, internet access, text editor, terminal and modern browser. Most tasks use free software or local runtimes.
roadmap.final_outcome: A completed playable 2D/3D action or platformer game featuring player controls, enemy AI, collision physics, health/scoring UI, sound effects, and multi-level progression.
